items.originalTitle: STX Maintained by Wells Fargo -- Price Target Lowered to $865
items.originalSummary: Wells Fargo lowered Western Digital's price target to $450 and Seagate's to $865, while maintaining ‘Overweight’ ratings.The firm sees an attractive risk-reward setup, with durable revenue growth of 25% to 30%-plus and a path to gross margins of 60% to 65%-plus.Both stocks have faced heavy selling pressure amid concerns that Toshiba's planned production expansion could threaten the industry's pricing power.Western Digital Corp. (WDC) and Seagate Technology Holdings Plc (STX) are on track to end their third consecutive week in the red, but Wells Fargo sees an opportunity in the hard disk drive makers’ steep selloff, even as it slashed their price targets by as much as 38% on Friday.According to The Fly, Wells Fargo cut Western Digital's price target to $450 from $730 and Seagate's to $865 from $1,180, while maintaining 'Overweight' ratings on both stocks.Over the last five trading sessions, WDC shares have fallen around 10%, while STX has plunged nearly 12%. Yet, the analyst remains bullish on the industry's fundamentals. The recent underperformance has created an attractive risk-reward setup heading into September-quarter earnings, TheFly noted, citing Wells Fargo. The firm continues to see durable revenue growth of 25% to 30% or more and a path toward gross margins of 60% to 65% or higher.At the time of this writing, WDC stock was down nearly 2%, while STX was also trading over 1% lower in Friday’s premarket session.Why WDC, STX Have Plunged LatelyWells Fargo's outlook comes amid a sharp selloff in data-storage stocks and broader weakness in AI-linked stocks, as investors question the sustainability of infrastructure spending amid higher borrowing costs and increasing scrutiny of returns on AI investments.Earlier this month, both WDC and STX came under pressure on October 2 after Nikkei reported that Japanese rival Toshiba planned to double production capacity for hard drives used in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers by fiscal 2027.The reported expansion, backed by an investment of approximately $380 million, raised concerns that additional supply could weaken the pricing power and profit margins Western Digital and Seagate have enjoyed amid strong AI-driven storage demand.What Last Earnings Report ShowsThe companies' latest financial results illustrate the growth underpinning Wells Fargo's outlook.In August, Western Digital reported fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) revenue growth of 44% year over year to $3.75 billion, with adjusted gross margin reaching 54.4%.Meanwhile, in July, Seagate reported fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) revenue of $3.63 billion, up approximately 48.5% year over year, while adjusted gross margin reached 52.7%.What Comes Next?Western Digital is scheduled to report fiscal first-quarter 2027 results on October 22, followed by Seagate on October 27.Both companies previously guided for quarterly revenue of approximately $4.1 billion. items.title: Project Suncatcher：Google在太空建立人工智慧資料中心的計畫解釋
items.originalTitle: Project Suncatcher: Google’s plan to setup an AI data centre in space explained
items.originalSummary: On October 1, 2026, a small satellite carrying four of Google’s AI chips rode a SpaceX Falcon 9 into low Earth orbit. Hours later, Google’s team confirmed contact and reported that the spacecraft was working as expected. It is not a data center, and it is not close to being one. It is the first piece of hardware for Project Suncatcher , Google’s research moonshot to run machine learning on solar-powered satellites, and it turns a long-running thought experiment about moving AI infrastructure into orbit into a mission engineers can actually measure. The timing is not accidental. AI’s appetite for electricity is colliding with grid limits, land constraints, and growing public resistance to data centers. This guide covers what Project Suncatcher is, what Google launched, the hurdles that stand between a four-chip prototype and a working orbital data center, and why getting answers back down to Earth may be the hardest problem of all.

investorBrief.event: 2026 年 10 月 1 日，一顆搭載四顆 Google AI 晶片的小型衛星搭乘 SpaceX Falcon 9 進入近地軌道。它不是一個資料中心，也遠遠不是一個資料中心。人工智慧對電力的需求正在與電網限制、土地限制以及公眾對資料中心日益增長的抵制發生衝突。本指南介紹了 Suncatcher 專案是什麼、Google 推出了什麼、四晶片原型和工作軌道資料中心之間存在的障礙，以及為什麼將答案傳回地球可能是最困難的
investorBrief.why: 真正的投資重點是 AI 資料中心的電力需求正在變成算力擴張瓶頸。大型科技公司若開始直接參與電力供給，通常對核電、電網、電力設備與資料中心基礎建設需求偏正面。
investorBrief.stance: 2026 年 10 月 1 日，一顆搭載四顆 Google AI 晶片的小型衛星搭乘 SpaceX Falcon 9 進入近地軌道。幾個小時後，Google團隊確認了聯繫，並報告說太空船正在按預期工作。它不是一個資料中心，也遠遠不是一個資料中心。它是 Suncatcher 項目的第一塊硬件，該項目是谷歌在太陽能衛星上運行機器學習的研究登月計劃，它將一項長期運行的關於將人工智能基礎設施移入軌道的思想實驗轉變為工程師可以實際測量的任務。這個時機並非偶然。人工智慧對電力的需求正在與電網限制、土地限制以及公眾對資料中心日益增長的抵制發生衝突。本指南介紹了 Suncatcher 專案是什麼、Google 推出了什麼、四晶片原型和工作軌道資料中心之間存在的障礙，以及為什麼要得到答案

historyItems.summary: GlobalFoundries Inc 計劃在日本政府高達 210 億美元的支持下建造兩座新的晶片工廠，其中美國還持有該公司 4% 的股份。根據週三宣布的一項協議，GlobalFoundries 將在其位於紐約州北部的工廠運營由美國和日本共同擁有的工廠。這些設施的資金來自日本承諾向美國投資 5,500 億美元的資金。這些工廠將生產所謂的基本晶片，即用於車輛、工業設備和通訊設備的重要但不太複雜的半導體。
historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries Gets $21 Billion for Plants in US-Japan Deal
historyItems.originalSummary: GlobalFoundries Inc plans to build two new chip plants with the backing of as much as US$21 billion from the Japanese government, part of an arrangement that also includes the US taking a 4 percent stake in the company. Under an agreement announced on Wednesday, GlobalFoundries will operate factories at its site in upstate New York that are jointly owned by the US and Japan. The facilities will be funded with money from Japan’s pledge to invest US$550 billion in the US. The factories will make so-called essential chips, the vital yet less sophisticated semiconductors used in vehicles, industrial equipment and communications gear. Photo: John Carl D’Annibale, The Albany Times Union via AP The GlobalFoundries agreement is meant to boost American production of essential chips and reduce dependence on East Asian suppliers — addressing a national security concern for the US. Under a broader arrangement with GlobalFoundries, the US Department of Commerce will take a roughly 4 percent equity stake in the company, “further enabling the American public to share in GF’s growth.” GlobalFoundries will get to redirect funds from a previous US CHIPS and Science Act grant to invest in honing its manufacturing abilities. That includes advancing its work in fields such as silicon photonics, chip packaging and silicon germanium. In a separate statement, the US Department of Commerce said it was reallocating US$955 million in CHIPS Act incentives to go toward GlobalFoundries’ factory expansion and modernization. As part of the agreement, the company will devote US$5 billion to capital investments at its plants in New York and Vermont. The new Japan-linked factories will be operated in the same way that GlobalFoundries runs its current facilities, which serve customers such as Apple Inc and Japanese firms including Renesas Electronics Corp. Profits will be divided among the owners and GlobalFoundries, following an approach laid out in last year’s US trade deal with Japan. US President Donald Trump touted the accord on his Truth Social site, saying it would help revitalize America’s industrial base and create jobs.

historyItems.originalTitle: Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'
historyItems.originalSummary: Dell shares plunged 11% on Wednesday, leading a data center equipment sell-off on mounting concerns that enterprise AI spending will not justify the AI buildout. Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle and Super Micro also declined. Barclays analysts downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to the equivalent of hold from buy in a Wednesday report to clients. The analysts cited enterprise AI timing after significant stock gains. Barclays analysts said enterprise spending at Dell, HPE and NetApp had not shown a meaningful acceleration related to AI. The analysts instead attributed increased revenue to the global memory shortage. The analysts noted that infrastructure companies had passed higher memory prices on to customers. Barclays analysts said businesses typically allocate just 5% of IT budgets to AI, despite growing expectations that enterprise AI adoption will drive hardware replacement. The analysts found that only about a quarter of total enterprise AI spending goes toward hardware. The analysts said normalizing and eventually declining memory prices could weigh on infrastructure-related revenue. Data center server and other backend equipment makers have attracted investor interest this year on expectations of large equipment sales linked to AI demand for years ahead. Dell shares have risen more than 300% this year, making Dell one of the market's top performers. HPE shares have risen about 160% this year. NetApp shares have doubled this year. However, sentiment toward AI infrastructure has shifted recently, partly because of concerning revenue figures from OpenAI. Investors also fear that rising interest rates will create difficulties because much of the AI buildout relies on debt. Oracle, a heavy borrower, fell 9% on Wednesday and is now down 33% for the year. Neocloud company CoreWeave plunged 15% on Wednesday, erasing CoreWeave's gains for 2026. Memory is a highly cyclical business. Memory stocks fell this week after China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, also known as CXMT, reported progress over the weekend on a new chip structure. Micron shares are down 11% for the week. South Korea's SK Hynix has fallen 13% in U.S. trading this week. Western Digital has dropped more than 8% this week.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to open 2 new chip plants in New York with $21 billion in financing from Japan
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to Build Two Chip Plants With Up to $21 Billion Funding
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: Palantir and London mayor's office settle lawsuit over UK police contract
historyItems.originalSummary: In the United Kingdom, US technology company Palantir and the office of London Mayor Sadiq Khan have settled the company’s lawsuit over the decision not to approve a contract with London police worth £50 million, or $66 million. Channel NewsAsia reports , citing a joint statement by the parties. Palantir agreed with London police on a two-year contract to use artificial intelligence systems. They were intended to automate some tasks and help analyse evidence. However, London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime refused to approve the agreement. It told police that no open competition had been held for the contract. Reports said that Khan’s representative also expressed concerns that Palantir did not align with London’s values. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . In a joint statement, Palantir and London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime said they had settled the case and withdrawn their mutual allegations. The parties also said that the decision not to enter into the contract was not based on Palantir’s values or ethics, or on broader coverage of the company’s activities. The office said it does not and has never had a policy of refusing to enter into contracts with Palantir. The company may participate in future procurement procedures. The United Kingdom is also reviewing the National Health Service’s £330 million contract with Palantir. A parliamentary committee said there was a clear mismatch between the company and the United Kingdom’s values and recommended invoking an early termination clause. Louis Mosley, head of Palantir’s UK division, called the recommendation irresponsible.

historyItems.summary: 官方網站使用 .gov .gov 網站屬於美國官方政府組織。華盛頓特區——商務部 CHIPS 計畫辦公室已與 GlobalFoundries 達成協議，修改其現有獎勵，並根據《CHIPS 和科學法案》重新分配高達 9.55 億美元的激勵措施。該修正案將增加分配給 GlobalFoundries 位於紐約州馬耳他和佛蒙特州伯靈頓的半導體製造工廠的現代化和擴建的現有 CHIPS 計劃獎勵的部分。
historyItems.originalTitle: Department of Commerce Announces Agreement with GlobalFoundries to Amend Its Existing CHIPS Program Award and Reallocate $955 Million to Accelerate Investments in Silicon Photonics, Silicon-Germanium, and Advanced Packaging
historyItems.originalSummary: Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Office has agreed with GlobalFoundries to amend its existing award and reallocate up to $955 million in incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act. The amendment will increase the portion of an existing CHIPS Program award allocated to GlobalFoundries’ modernization and expansion of its semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Malta, NY and Burlington, VT. As part of the amendment, GlobalFoundries has agreed to expand its capital investment in these facilities to $5 billion. The total amount of the existing CHIPS Program award will not be increased. The investment will expand domestic manufacturing capacity for technologies increasingly critical to communications infrastructure and data centers, including silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies. “GlobalFoundries is expanding its investment to develop and manufacture critical semiconductor technologies enabling data center and high-performance compute infrastructure,” said Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director for Semiconductor Innovation and Investment at the Department of Commerce. “The CHIPS Program award supports GlobalFoundries efforts to onshore and accelerate the development of these important semiconductor components." GlobalFoundries is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling technologies from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GlobalFoundries delivers differentiated, power efficient, and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high growth markets. Click here to download the PDF version of this press release.

historyItems.originalTitle: Chip-Machine Supplier ASML Boosts Guidance for Third Time on Surging AI Demand
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru ASML Holding improved its annual forecasts for the third time this year and said it was looking at ways to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines even more as the race to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuels demand for advanced chips. The Dutch group is projecting annual sales between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros, equivalent to a range of $49.27 billion to $50.39 billion, compared with prior guidance of 43 billion euros to 45 billion euros. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched metric of pricing power and profitability--should come in at roughly 56%, compared with a previous guidance range of 54% to 56%. The revisions show how much ASML's fortunes have come to benefit from the build-out of data centers that turned chips into a red-hot commodity. Surging semiconductor demand means that ASML's clients like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics and Intel will need more of its machines so they can produce enough chips. ASML shares in Amsterdam gained more than 2% in European morning trading, consolidating ASML's lead as Europe's most valuable listed company. Its stock is up more than 80% over the past 12 months on a wave of investor fervor around AI and expectations that chips and semiconductor-making tools will remain in high demand for years to come. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," ASML Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet said. AI demand pushed up the cost of certain types of chips as companies hoard semiconductors to power data centers, leading to a supply squeeze. Micron Technology Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said last month that supplies of memory and storage chips would be much tighter in the coming years. In a bid to cash in on that tightness, ASML is seeking to increase production of its deep ultraviolet lithography tools as well as its more advanced extreme ultraviolet systems. In July, it had earmarked a 30% boost in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. However, Fouquet said it was becoming clear that wouldn't be enough to meet demand and that ASML was looking at ways to bolster capacity even more, especially for 2028 and beyond. Earlier this year, ASML executives alluded to the possibility of price increases, saying that a tight chip market gave ASML more negotiating power. Finance chief Roger Dassen said that while the company had now completed conversations with key customers, the effect of higher prices wouldn't show on 2026 figures. "It will start to become visible partly in the course of 2027. The full impact of that you will start to see in 2028 and beyond," he said. ASML posted sales of 11.66 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 7.52 billion euros a year earlier. historyItems.originalTitle: Arista Networks (ANET) Stock Forecast and Price Target 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: Arista Networks (ANET) has put high-density AI infrastructure at the center of its story with a new open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, aiming to link accelerators across liquid-cooled racks for large-scale workloads. The latest AI rack-scale launch lands after a strong run in Arista Networks' shares, with the stock up 15.51% on a 90-day share price return and 57.84% year to date, while long-term total shareholder return over five years is about 8x. At a last close of US$210.88, the 1-day share price return fell 2.70% even as the 30-day gain of 5.66% and 1-year total shareholder return of 43.02% indicate ongoing momentum, supported by prior interest in Arista's 800G switching products and growing attention on AI infrastructure demand.

historyItems.originalTitle: Is Applied Materials (AMAT) A Bargain Following Its EPIC Center Launch?
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Materials (AMAT) just cut the ribbon on its EPIC Center in Sunnyvale, a US$5b semiconductor R&D hub that pulled the stock into focus after a modest premarket pullback. For investors, the near term has been choppy for Applied Materials, with the share price down 1.87% over the last session and 8.25% over the week. However, that pullback sits against a sharp year-to-date share price gain of 85.04% and a 1-year total shareholder return of 127.94%, which points to strong longer term momentum even as sentiment cools ahead of earnings and as the EPIC Center and recent AI-focused partnerships reset expectations around future opportunity and risk.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Lifts Off for Thursday Cargo Delivery
historyItems.originalSummary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station. Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS. The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

historyItems.title: Celestica 推出具有共同封裝光學元件的 DS6005 資料中心交換機，以實現高能源效率的 AI 結構
historyItems.summary: 多倫多，2026 年 10 月 12 日 (環球通訊社) -- 資料中心基礎設施和先進技術解決方案領域的全球領導者 Celestica Inc.（紐約證券交易所代碼：CLS）（多倫多證券交易所代碼：CLS）今天推出了 Celestica DS6005，這是一款共同安全性封裝 (CPO) 數據交換中心，旨在滿足網路數據中心，旨在滿足新功率、新層次 (CPO) 數據空間和新功率的系統。 DS6005 基於 Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson 交換器晶片構建，旨在以專為 OCP ORv3 機架設計的緊湊 1.5OU 外形尺寸提供高達 102.4Tbps 的交換容量。
historyItems.originalTitle: Celestica Introduces the DS6005 Data Center Switch with Co-Packaged Optics to Enable Power-Efficient AI Fabrics
historyItems.originalSummary: TORONTO, Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Celestica Inc. (NYSE: CLS) (TSX: CLS), a global leader in data center infrastructure and advanced technology solutions, today introduced the Celestica DS6005 , a co-packaged optics (CPO) data center switching system designed to address the bandwidth density, power, latency, and reach requirements of next-generation AI data center networks. Built on the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip, the DS6005 is designed to deliver up to 102.4Tbps of switching capacity in a compact 1.5OU form factor designed for OCP ORv3 racks. By co-packaging optical engines with the switch ASIC, the DS6005 eliminates the need for traditional front-panel pluggable optics, helping data center operators optimize bandwidth density, reduce latency, and improve power efficiency in the AI data center. “AI infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for bandwidth, while power, thermal management, latency, and reach are becoming increasingly important constraints,” said Gavin Cato, SVP & GM Portfolio Solutions & AI Platform Engineering, Celestica. “The DS6005 brings co-packaged optics, liquid cooling, field-replaceable external laser modules, and CPO-aware software management together in a compact platform designed to help customers build scalable and power-efficient AI fabrics.” Purpose-built to support AI/ML scale up and scale out networking, the DS6005 is a fully liquid-cooled, co-packaged optics data center switch that slashes power consumption and improves cluster efficiency while lowering latency and increasing reliability for next-generation AI clusters.

historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX ( SPCX ) isn't going quietly into what could be an eventful 2027. Elon Musk's rocket business said late last week it acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio . It positions Musk's satellite business, Starlink, to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US. Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tanked on the news on Friday. Meanwhile, SpaceX is reportedly seeking to raise $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips. "The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "We think the contracted backlog in AI and the cash generation of Starlink give SpaceX the capacity to service it, and we would rather see this compute financed and deployed than deferred."

historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia to start dealing out GPUs in high-stakes AI-RAN gamble
historyItems.originalSummary: Some drivers are happy to run a car until the chassis has corroded and the engine coughs with every agonizing change of gear. Others less constrained by economic circumstances want a new vehicle every time the paint is nicked. Many big telcos currently seem to have more in common with the first group, determined to run their mobile networks until the basestations are shrouded in cobwebs. Any upgrades, including to 6G, should not have to require hardware replacement, they are telling vendors. Yet Nokia wants to sell them a completely new engine. The Finnish company has publicly teamed up with Nvidia to design radio access network (RAN) products built on the giant chipmaker's graphics processing units (GPUs). It has stopped developing new custom silicon with partner Marvell Technology, although it will continue to support its existing 4G and 5G range for years. Ultimately, however, customers will have to buy new hardware to enjoy new features. There is no guarantee the situation will be all that different for customers of Ericsson. Operators using its purpose-built 5G products today may need to invest in newer application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to support forthcoming 5G-Advanced and 6G software. But Nokia's GPU strategy is undoubtedly much riskier. While commonplace in data centers and certain gadgets, Nvidia's chips have never been used for RAN compute. If telcos balk at the idea, Nokia could be in trouble. "If you don't have a companion strategy that's based on classic ASICs, you really have created jeopardy, I think," said Marcus Weldon, a former Nokia chief technology officer who was also president of its Bell Labs research unit. Yet the rewards could be immense if Nokia can prove that GPUs have advantages over ASICs in the RAN. In recent months, it has argued that its GPU-led strategy will support a doubling in spectral efficiency, among other benefits, by 2028. In a RAN market that is not expected to grow in the next few years, such improvements could justify the initial hardware outlay and even translate into market share gains for Nokia, allowing it to recover 5G ground lost to Ericsson and Samsung. That could be a disaster for Nokia's rivals. Numerous operators are now giving Nokia's AI-RAN products a test drive before they become commercially available early next year. None has yet said anything in public about the initial experience, and many operators have previously voiced concern about using what is still perceived to be a very expensive and energy-hungry chip in the RAN. Overkill has been the word on some lips, as if putting a GPU in the RAN is like using a rocket launcher to kill a rat. But Nokia has been advertising a slimline GPU that could be slotted into an existing Airscale chassis originally designed to support Marvell Technology's silicon. It will have to function with the same power constraints and be available for the same price, according to executives. They have also promised it will support software upgrades and new AI algorithms for years – unlike any ASIC. historyItems.originalTitle: Intel and Applied Materials Just Deepened Their AI Partnership. Which Stock Looks Better Positioned?
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Materials Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT ) and Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ) announced on October 6 that they are expanding their partnership on next-generation AI chipmaking. The two will work together on transistors, the wiring that connects them, and advanced packaging. That includes Intel's Foveros technology for stacking chips in 3D. Teams will work out of Applied's EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel's research campus in Oregon. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the goal is to move new technology from the lab into high-volume U.S. production faster. The Intel deal adds another dimension to Applied Materials' growth story. But before judging AMAT by its valuation, see what Jim Cramer thinks investors may be missing .

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry, and AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon stocks are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Free versions of Photoshop, Premiere Pro, and Lightroom are an easy sell to anyone tired of paying Adobe. Add a developer who says he vibe-coded replacements for seven of the company’s apps, and the triumphant headline practically writes itself. Adobe can presumably start clearing its desk. Brandon Thomas’s Crafting Apps give that excitement something to work with. People can download the tools, inspect the source code, and find their way around familiar interfaces. AI chatbots have quietly become a go-to source for medical advice the extent that some are dangerously skipping real doctors. But when AI's health advice goes wrong, doctors may never see the exchange behind it. Researchers from Binghamton University, Stanford, Texas A&M, and Indiana University published a paper in Nature Health examining what happens after a chatbot gives you bad health information. Their biggest concern is not just that chatbots can be wrong. It is that those mistakes often leave no trace for doctors, researchers, or regulators to catch.

historyItems.summary: 馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 正在超越衛星互聯網，並大舉進軍美國無線市場。根據《華爾街日報》報道，該公司已同意從投資公司 Grain Management 購買蜂窩頻譜許可證，據稱這筆交易價值約 80 億美元，這是該公司迄今為止與 AT&T、Verizon 和 T-Mobile 等老牌行動營運商競爭的最大舉措。該協議涉及 800MHz 頻段的頻譜，該頻段用於透過蜂窩塔等地面基礎設施提供的行動服務，而不是衛星。如果收購獲得批准，SpaceX 可以將這些無線電波與其不斷發展的 Starlink 衛星網路結合起來，創造更全面的無線服務。
historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies are reportedly preparing for a potential AI disaster that could turn the public against artificial intelligence. According to an Axios report, industry leaders are privately running through possible scenarios for what happens after a catastrophic AI incident. What kind of AI disaster are companies preparing for? AI is a useful tool for handling many tasks in private as well as professional settings, but medical advice, especially diagnosis, is one area where I generally draw the line. General-purpose chatbots tend to sound confident and convincing while giving medical advice, even when they are wrong, as studies have previously found. That being said, Google's new research points to a much more convincing use for AI in healthcare. Its Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer chatbot, or AMIE for short, could help prepare both sides before the appointment even begins.

historyItems.title: TELUS 整合進度導致 AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 估值可能被低估 67%
historyItems.summary: 在公司和 TELUS 完成首次整合測試後，AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 重新成為人們關注的焦點，該測試將 TELUS 的地面無線網路與 AST SpaceMobile 的衛星系統連接起來，在加拿大提供智慧型手機直接到衛星服務。 AST SpaceMobile 與 TELUS 的整合取得進展是在該公司股票經歷波動之後，該公司股價在過去一天下跌了 6.13%，在過去一個月下跌了 13.90%，導致今年迄今為止下跌了 31.80%。與上市初期相比，三年和五年的長期股東總回報仍然非常高，這表明近期的疲軟反映了風險預期的變化，而不是更廣泛的多年走勢的簡單逆轉。
historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) Could Be 67% Undervalued On TELUS Integration Progress
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) moved back into focus after the company and TELUS completed their first integration test connecting TELUS' terrestrial wireless network with AST SpaceMobile's satellite based system for direct smartphone to satellite service in Canada. AST SpaceMobile's integration progress with TELUS comes after a volatile run for the stock, with the share price falling 6.13% over the past day and 13.90% over the past month, contributing to a 31.80% decline in the year to date. Long term total shareholder return over three and five years remains very large compared with the initial listing period, suggesting recent weakness reflects shifting risk expectations rather than a simple reversal of the broader multi year move.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA Sets Coverage for SpaceX 35th Station Resupply Launch, Arrival
historyItems.originalSummary: A SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft departs from the International Space Station on June 16 after undocking from the Harmony module's forward port. Dragon, packed with completed science experiments and cargo for retrieval and analysis on Earth, parachuted to a splashdown off the coast of southern California the following day.NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, to the space station. This is the 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the orbital complex for NASA.NASA also will host a media teleconference on Thursday, Oct. 8 that will preview the cargo resupply flight, as well as provide a post-splashdown update for the agency's SpaceX Crew-12 mission, which will have returned to Earth from the space station Thursday morning.Loaded with more than 6,300 pounds of supplies, a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Dragon will dock autonomously around 11 a.m. on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station's Harmony module.NASA's live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:https://www.nasa.gov/liveIn addition to the solar arrays, the Dragon spacecraft will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissues models to advance large-scale drug testing on future missions. The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and multiple sclerosis.The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart the orbiting laboratory and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.NASA's mission coverage is as follows (all times Eastern and subject to change based on real-time operations):Thursday, Oct. 81:15 p.m.: International Space Station briefing for Crew-12 return, and SpaceX's 35th Commercial Resupply Services launch with the following participants:Bill Spetch, deputy manager of Commercial, Low Earth Orbit ProgramDr. Liz Warren, deputy chief scientist, NASA's International Space Station OfficeLee Echerd, senior mission manager, Customer Operations and Integration, SpaceXAndreas Mogensen, leader, Human Exploration Group, ESA (European Space Agency)To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 12 p.m., Oct. 8, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. historyItems.originalTitle: Judge could order Nebius to halt data center construction in Independence
historyItems.originalSummary: A motions hearing is set for Oct. 22 on a lawsuit related to the Nebius data center project in Independence.The Independence GUARD (Guardians United Against Reckless Development) Alliance filed the lawsuit to halt construction of the Nebius hyperscale AI data factory in the Little Blue Valley.Named in the lawsuit are the city of Independence, Missouri ADC Holdings LLC (data center developer) and Independence Power Partners LP.Residents along Bly Road in the Little Blue Valley are hoping to stop construction near their homes.The lawsuit alleges the city violated zoning and sunshine laws, as well as the city charter, and has failed to enforce city laws. Residents are asking a judge to pause the project.A hearing has been set for 9 a.m. on Oct. 22 on their motion for a temporary restraining order and the defendants' motion to dismiss.The Independence City Council approved billions of dollars in incentives for Dutch tech company Nebius to build and operate the 2.1-million-square-foot hyperscale AI data factory on 400 acres at the south end of Bly Road in March. Nebius broke ground on the first phase of the project in April.Nebius — which is party to the lawsuit through a subsidiary, Missouri ADC Holdings — provided us a statement about the lawsuit when it was filed earlier this year in Jackson County Circuit Court.“We are reviewing the claims and cannot comment on the case specifics,” Nebius Vice President of Public Affairs John Sutter said in a statement. “Nebius remains committed to complying with all applicable laws and regulations, and being a responsible partner for the community as our historic investment in Independence takes shape.”—

The letter can be downloaded here. In the third quarter, leadership among large growth stocks shifted from high-momentum semiconductor names to companies with clearer AI monetization paths. The ClearBridge Large Cap Growth Strategy outperformed its Russell 1000 Growth Index benchmark, benefiting from strong stock selection and disciplined valuation approaches. Despite volatility and a selloff in higher-beta AI stocks, the S&P 500 Index and NASDAQ Composite posted gains. The benchmark Russell 1000 Growth Index posted a modest gain of 0.9% while the Russell 1000 Value Index was up 2.6%. The Strategy broadened exposure across select semiconductor, AI infrastructure, and diversifying growth companies, while maintaining measured momentum exposure. historyItems.summary: Teradyne, Inc. 宣布推出一款可投入生產的系統，可在其 Titan? 上提供增強的預燒功能？惠普平台。傳統的老化會將設備在受控空氣溫度下的專用烘箱中保存數小時，然後再進行功能測試。相反，Teradyne Titan HP 在運行實際設備工作負載時將每個設備保持在其目標結溫，從而優化可靠性應力功能，並在每個設備級別啟用熱控制。
historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne enhances Titan HP for AI chip reliability tests
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne, Inc. announced a production-ready system that delivers enhanced burn-in capabilities on its Titan? HP platform. Traditional burn-in holds devices in banks of dedicated ovens at a controlled air temperature for hours before they move on to functional test.Teradyne Titan HP instead holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, so reliability stress functions are optimized and thermal controls are enabled at the per-device level. Titan HP can be used for system level test or reliability testing, optimizing capital cost investments. For reliability testing, every device carries its full stress-and-test history on a single record.Per-site thermal control, tuned to each device's thermal and force zones, and paired with high per-device kilowatt power delivery, lets Titan HP sustain reliability-stress conditions on parts whose power draw and heat dissipation strain a conventional oven flow. The platform's asynchronous slot architecture loads and tests each slot independently, so a long stress run on one device does not idle the rest of the system, and individual sites can be serviced while the system continues to operate. Test programs run on the Teradyne Atlas software platform, which lets engineers import existing programs or build new ones and port them to other Teradyne system level test systems. Burn-in has long been standard for automotive and other high-reliability silicon.AI accelerators and cloud infrastructure devices are now entering the same category, driven by the high cost of a single failed accelerator in a deployed rack. Enhanced burn-in extends Teradyne?s test portfolio, which spans the AI device supply chain from wafer to data center.

historyItems.originalTitle: Is Planet Labs PBC (PL) Cheap Following Its 20 Satellite Launches?
historyItems.originalSummary: Planet Labs PBC (PL) just put 20 more satellites into orbit, including a prototype for Google's Project Suncatcher and the hyperspectral Tanager-2. This development raises fresh questions about how this build-out might affect the stock. Recent product milestones have arrived against a tougher tape for Planet Labs PBC. The 1-day share price return declined 0.8% to US$17.36 and the 90-day share price return fell 39.4%, even though the 1-year total shareholder return is 13.9% and the 3-year total shareholder return is roughly 7x. This suggests the market is reassessing near term risk even as longer term holders remain ahead.

historyItems.originalTitle: Marvell raises 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data center demand
historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell raised its 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, citing strong demand for its chips used in data centers.Shares of the company rose nearly 9% in early trading. The stock has more than tripled in value so far this year.Marvell had forecast $18 billion in revenue in August. Analysts were expecting revenue of $18.2 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

historyItems.title: Marvell 將 2028 年營收預期上調至 200 億美元，股價飆升
historyItems.summary: 資料中心連接和客製化人工智慧晶片製造商 Marvell Technology（納斯達克股票代碼：MRVL）收在 287.01 美元，上漲 5.81%。投資者對投資者日指引做出了反應，該指引提高了近期和長期收入目標，他們正在關注下一步定制人工智慧的成長。交易量達到 5,010 萬股，比三個月平均 2,260 萬股高出約 122%。 Marvell Technology 於 2000 年首次公開募股，自上市以來已成長 1,927%。
historyItems.originalTitle: Marvell stock surges after company raises 2028 revenue outlook to $20 billion
historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a data-center connectivity and custom AI chipmaker, closed at $287.01, up 5.81%. Investors were reacting to Investor Day guidance that lifted near- and long-term revenue targets, and they are watching custom AI growth next. Trading volume reached 50.1 million shares, coming in about 122% above its three-month average of 22.6 million shares. Marvell Technology IPO'd in 2000 and has grown 1,927% since going public.

historyItems.originalTitle: AMD plans to substantially increase supply in 2027, CEO says
historyItems.originalSummary: AMD plans to increase its chip supply in 2027 as the company works to keep pace with demand for artificial intelligence hardware, chair and CEO Lisa Su said Tuesday, according to Reuters . "We've been able to increase our supply as we've gone through 2026, and we're going to substantially increase our supply in 2027, but we can definitely use more," Su told reporters in Taipei.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX jumps to highest close since June on bullish Morgan Stanley call
historyItems.originalSummary: After reaching highs in the initial days following its mid-June IPO, SpaceX SPCX shares fell sharply, declining about 48% through late July. historyItems.originalTitle: KLA (KLAC) Stock Looks Rich As Revenue Guidance Rises
historyItems.originalSummary: In recent days, KLA Corporation has attracted renewed attention as analysts highlighted its essential process-control role in easing the chip shortage and supporting AI-focused semiconductor manufacturing, while also pointing to ongoing risks from U.S. export restrictions and cyclical wafer equipment spending. At the same time, upward revisions to earnings estimates and commentary about KLA's differentiated tools for advanced packaging and complex chip designs have reinforced the company's importance to AI infrastructure build-outs, even as investors weigh exposure to tariffs, component costs, and concentrated customer demand. We'll now examine how this stronger analyst sentiment around KLA's critical AI-related process-control demand reshapes and reinforces its existing investment narrative.

historyItems.title: NASA 將直播 SpaceX Crew-12 回歸、Splashdown 直播
historyItems.summary: Crew-12 的四名成員已在太空生活了近八個月，他們最早將於週三離開國際太空站。美國太空總署太空人傑西卡·梅爾和傑克·海瑟薇、歐洲太空總署太空人索菲·阿德爾諾特和俄羅斯太空總署太空人安德烈·費德亞耶夫四人於 2 月 13 日乘坐 SpaceX 載人龍自由號從卡納維拉爾角太空部隊站發射升空。不過，隨著 Crew-13 上週抵達國際太空站，他們已經向新船員展示了他們的軌道家園，並準備返回地球。
historyItems.originalTitle: NASA to Stream SpaceX Crew-12 Return, Splashdown Live
historyItems.originalSummary: With nearly eight months in space under their belt, the four members of Crew-12 are set to depart the International Space Station as early as Wednesday. The quartet of NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station back on Feb. 13 riding up in the SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom. With the arrival of Crew-13 to the station last week, though, they have shown the new crew around their orbiting home and are ready to make their way back to Earth.

historyItems.originalTitle: Homeowners seek subpoena for mayor’s wife’s realty company in Nebius data center suit
historyItems.originalSummary: Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin is pushing back after his wife and her real-estate company were named in a discovery dispute tied to a lawsuit over a proposed Birmingham data center. In a statement posted to Facebook Wednesday, Woodfin said his wife, Kendra Woodfin, and her company, Iron City Premier Realty, had no involvement in the purchase or sale of the property where the Nebius data center is planned. “Here we go again,” Woodfin said. “This is a bald-faced lie. “My wife and her business had nothing to do with this property. She had no part in the purchase. No part in the sale. No connection to this litigation. There isn't a shred of evidence that says otherwise, because there's nothing to find. She wasn't involved. Period.” The comments follow an Oct. 6 filing in Jefferson County Circuit Court in which Iron City objected to a proposed subpoena from homeowners challenging the data-center project. Iron City said it “had no involvement” in the acquisition, purchase, sale, conveyance, financing, brokerage, development, zoning, permitting or closing of the property identified in the subpoena. The company also argued the subpoena is overly broad and that the plaintiffs have not established a factual basis connecting Iron City to the transaction. The court has not ruled on the objections. Woodfin also emphasized that his wife is a private citizen and has no role in Birmingham's zoning or permitting decisions. “She is a business owner. She is the mother of our children. She is a private citizen. She has never held office in this city. She doesn't vote on zoning. She doesn't sign permits. She doesn't sit on the Zoning Board of Adjustment or the City Council,” he said. Woodfin accused the attorneys behind the filing of intentionally putting his wife's business name into the case because of her relationship to him. “They wanted a headline,” he said. “Everybody knows how politically charged and unpopular data centers are. That's the play. You put a name in a court filing. Reporters read court filings. The story writes itself: ‘Mayor's wife named in data center lawsuit.’” Woodfin said he plans to pursue legal options to protect his wife's reputation. “We are going to be as aggressive as possible, exploring every legal recourse available to protect my wife's good name and the professional reputation of her business. This won't be the last you hear about it.” The mayor said he is accustomed to criticism but does not want his wife drawn into political disputes. “Come at me all day. I've been taking hits for nine years, and I'll take plenty more. That's the job I signed up for. My wife didn't. And I won't let her become collateral damage in a political hit designed to get at me.” The underlying lawsuit was filed by homeowners Robert B. Sansome and Gail Sansome against Hoar Construction LLC, Lakeshore Data Center LLC, Nebius Inc. and the City of Birmingham. The case remains in discovery, with a non-jury trial scheduled for March 8, 2027. A judge is scheduled to hear arguments Wednesday on objections involving subpoenas. The latest filings do not establish that Kendra Woodfin or Iron City Premier Realty participated in the property transactions at issue.

historyItems.originalTitle: Kratos Reports More Than $100M in Contracts for Space Intelligence Data
historyItems.originalSummary: SAN DIEGO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced multiple contract awards totaling over $100 million to develop prototype mission applications and cyber capabilities providing space intelligence data in support of joint operations across the space and cyberspace domains. Work under the contracts will provide warfighters with capabilities to collect and process complex radio frequency (RF) signals, develop intelligence on the operational environment and support the joint targeting cycle – the process used to identify, prioritize and target assets. The prototype systems will support electronic warfare and offensive cyber operations, including capabilities for access and battle damage assessment. The work leverages the KnownSpace ® Network, Kratos’ global RF collection infrastructure consisting of more than 190 strategically placed sensors around the world, along with RF data and capabilities provided by KnownSpace Recon+™, Kratos’ field-portable space domain awareness (SDA) terminals. In addition, the contracts will leverage Kratos’ software products, analytics and expertise in RF, signal processing, cybersecurity and software development, establishing a proven technology base that can be adapted and integrated to meet emerging space and cyber mission requirements. “Kratos brings decades of space experience together with proven commercial technology and agile engineering to solve some of today’s most complex mission challenges,” said Greg Caicedo, Senior Vice President at Kratos . “Our systems, software and hardware support missions across SDA, command & control, satellite operations and cybersecurity. By building on proven technology and rapidly adapting it to emerging mission needs, we can deliver new capabilities faster and keep pace as the space environment changes.” The Kratos KnownSpace family of SDA products and services which support these awards provide deep insights for global, sovereign, and tactical operations. Built on more than 30 years of satellite monitoring and RF expertise, the KnownSpace family combines global RF sensing, software, managed operations and deployable systems to detect, characterize and understand satellite and terrestrial activity. Solutions include enterprise software applications, portable form factors that can be deployed anywhere and persistent global RF signal monitoring and geolocation through its KnownSpace Network of over 20 locations and 190 sensors worldwide—the largest commercially owned, commercially operated (COCO) RF sensor network.
